reason: The passage (Exodus 3) describes God hearing the צַעֲקַת (cry) of the Israelites suffering under Egyptian oppression and seeing (רָאִיתִי) their affliction (הַלַּחַץ). God's response is compassionate action—commissioning Moses to liberate them from slavery. The text contains no language indicating anger (אַף, חֲמָה, or כַּעַס) toward the people. Rather, God demonstrates concern for their suffering and initiates their redemption. The Israelites' cry is one of distress under oppression, not presumptuous voicing of opinions, and God's reaction is salvific, not wrathful.
